bug_semantics: An unauthenticated proxy client can put an arbitrary HTTP(S) origin in x-headroom-base-url. Headroom uses that origin as the upstream without establishing that its resolved addresses are public, forwards the incoming request headers and body to it, and returns the upstream response. A caller can therefore reach loopback, link-local/cloud-metadata, RFC 1918, and other internal services through the proxy and read their responses; the incoming Authorization header also follows the caller-selected destination. The reference compose deployment amplified reachability by publishing the proxy on 0.0.0.0 without requiring HEADROOM_PROXY_TOKEN.
flaw_origin: Commit 729cc035a474b4ff04c6c16c62d3a5f4e515c56f introduced the trust-boundary violation in headroom/proxy/server.py: the catch-all route read x-headroom-base-url and immediately passed custom_base.rstrip('/') to the pre-existing handle_passthrough method. That method copied all request headers except Host into the outbound request and relayed the response content/status/headers. The commit added no scheme, hostname, address-class, DNS, or operator-allowlist validation. Later commits moved the same catch-all mechanism and expanded it to dedicated OpenAI handlers; they did not originate the already exploitable SSRF.
ai_marker: absent on BIC 729cc035a474b4ff04c6c16c62d3a5f4e515c56f: git cat-file -p shows human author and committer chopratejas <chopratejas@gmail.com>, with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI-attribution trailer. The commit message discusses LLM-facing product behavior but does not attribute authorship to AI.
evidence: Advisory: GHSA-4j5r-9p93-j2px / CVE-2026-77775 names x-headroom-base-url, _resolve_openai_upstream_base in headroom/proxy/handlers/openai.py, and _select_passthrough_base_url / passthrough routes, and describes private-address SSRF, response disclosure, and Authorization forwarding; first-party PR #2207 identifies this as WEB-01. Origin search: git log --all --reverse -S'x-headroom-base-url' returned 729cc035a474b4ff04c6c16c62d3a5f4e515c56f as the repository's first occurrence (2026-02-18, 'Add compression summaries, multi-provider headers, Dockerfile fix'). Its diff at headroom/proxy/server.py:6572-6597 added custom_base = request.headers.get('x-headroom-base-url') and return await proxy.handle_passthrough(request, custom_base.rstrip('/')). At the same tree, headroom/proxy/server.py:4294-4353 shows handle_passthrough constructing url = f'{base_url}{path}', copying dict(request.headers.items()), removing only Host, calling http_client.request(... headers=headers ...), then returning response.content/status/headers. Parent absence: git grep -F 'x-headroom-base-url' 55d8fb63614f56fde11b871a9b1d088c43040946 returned no match, while the same command at 729cc035a474b4ff04c6c16c62d3a5f4e515c56f returned the two new server.py reads. The BIC is a direct one-parent commit, not a move or reconstructable squash; its commit page and object expose no PR-member chain. Lineage: the v0.29.0 assessment tree still has the unvalidated catch-all at headroom/providers/proxy_routes.py:996-998. c19347c31046bf25baf9b1a816c9bede5d3ee807 later added _resolve_openai_upstream_base and dedicated-handler calls that accept only syntactically valid HTTP(S) origins, expanding the vulnerable surface. git blame attributes the v0.29.0 catch-all text to 49a8f80e9b7c14c8e913e6160851f6f8fa8e0b3d, but that commit is a whole-file line-ending normalization with a Copilot trailer, so it is a later mechanical rewrite, not the BIC. Version boundary: merge-base checks show the BIC absent from v0.3.0, present in v0.3.7 (the BIC itself bumped the package version to 0.3.5, for which no tag exists), and present in advisory assessment tag v0.29.0. Initial fix 1f96dabc19130947770353cd6e814db4fd96e6a0 (#2207) added upstream_guard and reached v0.36.1, but it was incomplete: /v1/alpha/search still used the unguarded Azure branch of select_passthrough_base_url. First-party PR #3195 demonstrates that residual route reaching loopback, forwarding Authorization, and relaying the body. Complete mainline squash 3e3c409436792129259cfae3d95179a94321f9ce validates the selection chokepoints and alpha-search path and tightens the address policy; its patch is byte-identical to the combined PR-member diff 57b414373ea4904f98910b4edc91eebd6030c981 plus 1264580dee507fdf213e48653ab11711e62da0e9. Tag ancestry proves 3e3c409436792129259cfae3d95179a94321f9ce absent from v0.36.3 and present in v0.36.4, the first tag containing the complete fix. Fix-side Claude attribution on 3e3c409436792129259cfae3d95179a94321f9ce is not BIC evidence.
reasoning: The causal root is the first client-controlled destination selection, not the current file attribution. Commit 729cc035a474b4ff04c6c16c62d3a5f4e515c56f made a request header authoritative over the outbound origin while reusing a passthrough routine that forwards headers and discloses the response. Direct inspection of its immediate parent proves the header mechanism was absent. Later extraction/restoration and line-ending commits merely carried that behavior into provider routes; c19347c31046bf25baf9b1a816c9bede5d3ee807 broadened it to dedicated OpenAI routes. In particular, the Copilot-attributed 49a8f80e9b7c14c8e913e6160851f6f8fa8e0b3d is excluded because its relevant change is normalization of already-existing route code. The release graph is coherent: the origin lies between v0.3.0 and v0.3.7, is an ancestor of the assessed v0.29.0, and the complete fix lands only in v0.36.4 after the partial v0.36.1 guard missed one sink. BIC-only commit-object review finds a human author/committer and no AI marker on 729cc035a474b4ff04c6c16c62d3a5f4e515c56f. AI disclosure in fix PR bodies, the Claude trailer on the complete fix, and the later Copilot normalization cannot attribute the root cause. Therefore the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
